correctness.rationale: The positive-definite Schur factorization gives an independent planar translation-noise integral and an angular integral of (R_phi-I)a on each continuous excursion. Exponential renewal intervals yield E[e^{in phi_S}]=rho/(rho+n^2), all first and second joint reward/duration moments, and the explicitly compensated reward Y-vS. The regenerative covariance E[(Y-vS)(Y-vS)^T]/E S includes random-duration fluctuations and equals twice the stated diffusion tensor. Exponential inter-reset times and bounded angular excursion displacement control the residual at a non-reset observation endpoint; the renewal-reward CLT gives the Gaussian limit. Factorization of the longitudinal derivative and monotonicity of the switch polynomial prove the unique extremum and axis switch. 1,827 scalar tests, 289 generic exact matrix tests and 12 independent anisotropic path covariance tests passed in the included standalone verifier, including 450,000 full renewal excursions; numerical checks are auxiliary.

originality.rationale: The 2026 starting article gives the full coupled-mobility model and periodic-reset mean velocity, not the Poisson-clock centered covariance. Chaki et al. explicitly assume independent angular and translational driving noises, which means the cross block h=0: their Poisson-reset diffusivity is the noncoupled limit of the first line of our tensor, and cannot give the geometric covariance term or its anisotropy reversal. The prior generic hidden-coordinate renewal analysis provides a method but does not report the all-mobility formula or the sharp symmetric-Schur rate transition. Fixed-duration cycle covariance calculations are not themselves sufficient for random-duration centering; an additional reward-duration mixed moment is required. Primary full text was inspected for the two most plausible precedents; limited later primary access and possible alternative reductions are disclosed.

value.rationale: Directional spreading is an observable directly motivated in the 2026 physical sorting paper, which proposes diffusion enhancement and random protocols as further directions. A closed general tensor distinguishes the existing uncoupled anisotropic noise from a new mobility cross-term; an isotropic-Schur choice removes trivial body anisotropy and proves a genuine rate-induced eigenaxis reversal at one unique cubic root, while longitudinal spreading has its unique optimum at a different reset frequency. This clarifies distinct transport-control objectives and is not a mere parameter rename, arbitrary coefficient census, or marginal numerical improvement.
